claims.text: The name Bungo was meaningless in contemporary Hobbitish Westron. It represented an original name Bunga.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix F, "On Translation"

claims.text: Bungo was the eldest child of Mungo Baggins and Laura Grubb. He married Belladonna Took, daughter of the Old Took, towards . Bungo and Belladonna had only one child together, the famous Bilbo Baggins.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix C, "Baggins of Hobbiton"

claims.text: Father and son were so much alike, in looks and behaviour, that Bilbo seemed like a "second edition" of his "solid and comfortable" father.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "An Unexpected Party"

claims.text: Apart from fathering Bilbo, Bungo's other achievements were that he built and excavated the rather luxurious Bag End in the Hill in Hobbiton and that he laid down several bottles of Old Winyards wine that would be enjoyed by Rorimac Brandybuck after Bilbo's Farewell Party and by the small party on 21 September that Frodo Baggins gave before leaving Bag End.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "An Unexpected Party"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Fellowship of the Ring, "Three is Company"

claims.text: Bungo had an aptitude for either remembering or coining proverbs. Bilbo quoted his father's sayings "third time pays for all" before making his first descent into Erebor, "Every worm has his weak spot" while talking to the Dragon Smaug, and "while there's life there's hope" when leading the Dwarves down to Smaug's lair.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Inside Information"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Not at Home"
